items.title: The Sixteen Practices Re-Explained Through the Path of Cultivation

items.zh: 問：如是十六差別云何？答：有學見迹已得四念住等，於入出息所緣作意復更進修，為斷餘結。是故念言：於念入息，我今能學念於入息；於念出息，我今能學念於出息。若緣入息、出息境時，便作念言：我今能學念長入息、念長出息。若緣中間入息、中間出息境時，便作念言：我今能學念短入息、念短出息。如入息出息長轉，及中間入息、中間出息短轉，即如是了知。如是名為若長、若短。若緣身中微細孔穴，入息、出息周遍隨入諸毛孔中，緣此為境，起勝解時，便作念言：我於覺了遍身入息出息，我今能學覺了遍身入息出息。若於是時，或入息、中間入息已滅，出息、中間出息未生，緣入息出息空無位、入息出息遠離位為境；或出息、中間出息已滅，入息、中間入息未生，緣出息入息空無位、出息入息遠離位為境。即於此時便作念言：於息除身行入息，我今能學息除身行入息；於息除身行出息，我今能學息除身行出息。又即於此若修、若習、若多修習為因緣故，先未串習入出息時，所有剛強苦觸隨轉，今已串習入出息故，皆得息除，有餘柔軟樂觸隨轉。便作念言：於息除身行入息，我今能學息除身行入息；於息除身行出息，我今能學息除身行出息。又於如是阿那波那念勤修行者，若得初靜慮，或得第二靜慮時，便作念言：於覺了喜入息出息，我今能學覺了喜入息出息。若得離喜第三靜慮時，便作念言：於覺了樂入息出息，我今能學覺了樂入息出息。第三靜慮已上，於阿那波那念無有更修加行道理，是故乃至第三靜慮，宣說息念加行所攝。又即如是覺了喜者、覺了樂者，或有暫時生起忘念。或謂有我我所，或發我慢，或謂我當有，或謂我當無，或謂我當有色，或謂我當無色，或謂我當有想，或謂我當無想，或謂我當非有想非無想。生起如是愚癡想思俱行種種動慢、戲論、造作、貪愛；纔生起已，便能速疾以慧通達，不深染著，方便斷滅、除遣、變吐。由是加行，便作念言：於覺了心行入息出息，我今能學覺了心行入息出息；於息除心行入息出息，我今能學息除心行入息出息。又若得根本第一、第二、第三靜慮，彼定已得初靜慮近分未至依定，依此觀察所生起心。謂如實知、如實覺了，或有貪心、或離貪心、或有瞋心、或離瞋心、或有癡心、或離癡心、略心、散心、下心、舉心、有掉動心、無掉動心、有寂靜心、無寂靜心、有等引心、無等引心、善修習心、不善修習心、善解脫心、不善解脫心。
items.en: Question: What are the distinctions among these sixteen? Answer: A trainee who has already seen the trace of the path — having attained the four foundations of mindfulness and so on — further advances the attentive object of the in-breath and out-breath in order to cut off the remaining fetters. … And having attained the actual first, second, or third absorption — which entails also having attained the preparatory stage bordering the first absorption — one observes, based on this, whatever mind arises: truly knowing, truly recognising, whether it is a mind with desire or free of desire, with aversion or free of aversion, with delusion or free of delusion, contracted or scattered, sunken or lifted, agitated or unagitated, tranquil or untranquil, absorbed or unabsorbed, well-cultivated or poorly cultivated, well-liberated or not yet liberated.

blocks.text: The treatise now explains the sixteen practices one by one. Ru-Yi translates the first part (in abbreviated form; the English row compresses a long passage); tomorrow's continuation is untranslated.

"A trainee who has already seen the trace of the path, having attained the four foundations of mindfulness, further advances the attentive object of the breath in order to cut off the remaining fetters." Venerable Miào Jìng: the earlier breath practice is for ordinary beings; the sixteen are for those after stream-entry.

Most of this passage is in the Chinese column only; in brief: "long" breath means the full in- and out-breath; "short" means the faint mid-interval breath. Awareness "through the whole body" is attending to the breath entering and leaving through every pore. "Calming bodily activity" is attending to the gap where one breath has ceased and the next has not arisen; with practice, the harsh sensations of untrained breathing give way to soft, pleasant ones. With the first or second absorption one experiences **joy**; with the third, **pleasure**. Above the third absorption there is no further breath practice. If thoughts of "I", "mine", "I shall exist", "I shall not exist" arise, one sees through them at once and lets them go: this is awareness and calming of **mental activity**.

"One observes whatever mind arises, truly knowing whether it is a mind with desire or free of desire, with aversion or free of it, with delusion or free of it, contracted or scattered, sunken or lifted, agitated or unagitated, tranquil or untranquil, absorbed or unabsorbed, well cultivated or not, well liberated or not." Venerable Miào Jìng: a "contracted" mind (略心) is one sunk in dullness; when the mind is agitated and one restrains it, that is "lowering".
This list of mind-states, taken from the *Satipaṭṭhāna Sutta*, is a practical checklist. Simply noticing which state is present, without judgement, is the beginning of mastery over it.

quiz.q: Among the twenty minds, 略心 and 下心 are rendered "contracted" and "sunken." How do the lectures read them?
options: Miào Jìng: 略心 is torpor; 下心 is pressing down an agitated mind; Cháng Bǎi: a drowsy, torpid mind is 下心
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: what is 略心? Torpor and drowsiness. And when the mind is agitated and you restrain it, that is 下心. Master Cháng Bǎi: when the mind is torpid and drowsy, that is 下心. The two masters also differ on 下心.

quiz.q: Observing the mind relies only on the first three absorptions. Why not the fourth, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: from the fourth absorption up there is no breath, so this method is no longer practised
quiz.why: "Having attained the actual first, second, or third absorption … one observes, based on this, whatever mind arises." Venerable Miào Jìng: from the fourth absorption up there is no in- or out-breath, so this method is no longer practised.
